title: Paint Grab – Free Territory Painting Game vs Bots (No Sign-up)
description: Play Paint Grab free in your browser: paint the school yard, loop back to your colour to grab ground, and cut rival painters' trails before they cut yours.
body: You are a little paint blob in a sunny school yard. Step out of your colour and you leave a wet paint trail; loop back home and everything inside the loop becomes yours. While your trail is wet you are exposed: if a rival painter touches it, you splat.

Each round lasts two minutes against five to seven painter bots. Finish with the biggest share of the yard to win the round, then carry on to the next one, where the bots are faster and smarter. No text, no account, and it plays in portrait or landscape on phones, tablets, Chromebooks and desktops.
New here? Read how to play and the tips to grab more of the yard.

title: How to Play Paint Grab – Controls, Trails and Rounds
description: Paint Grab controls: drag to steer or use the arrow keys. Learn how trails, loops, eliminations, rounds, paint drops and the shop work.
body: Your painter never stops moving. On a phone or tablet, drag your finger anywhere on the screen in the direction you want to go: the spot where you touch becomes the centre of a small joystick. With a mouse, click and drag the same way. On a keyboard, use the arrow keys or WASD.

Inside your own colour you are safe. As soon as you step out, you leave a trail of wet paint. Come back to any part of your colour and the trail closes a loop: the trail and everything it surrounds is painted in your colour, even if it belonged to someone else.

Trails are the weak spot. If you run over a rival's trail, that painter is out and their colour disappears from the yard. If a rival runs over yours, you are out. Crossing your own trail also knocks you out, and if two painters bump heads, the one standing in its own colour wins.

The percentage at the top is how much of the yard you own, the medal shows your place, and the clock counts down the two-minute round. When it reaches zero you get paint drops for your share of the yard plus a bonus for the podium, and the next round starts with more, faster and smarter bots.

Spend paint drops in the shop (the bag button on the menu) on new painters and trail styles. There is also a daily gift that grows if you play on consecutive days. If the portal offers it, you can watch an optional video once per game to keep going after a splat, or to double your drops.

title: Paint Grab Tips: Grab More of the Yard Without Getting Cut
description: Practical tips to win more rounds in Paint Grab: short safe loops, reading the bots, cutting trails, using the walls and protecting your colour.
body: Short loops first. At the start your colour is tiny. Three or four quick rectangles grow it faster and much more safely than one huge loop.
Go wide along your own edge. A long thin loop that hugs your colour adds a lot of ground while keeping home only a few steps away.
Watch the heads, not the trails. A rival is only dangerous if it can reach your trail before you get home. When a painter turns towards you, head back.
Know the bots. Some painters make tiny careful squares; greedy ones draw big loops and are easy to cut; hunters come straight for long trails, especially yours.
Cut greedy painters. A long trail far from home is an easy target. Running over it removes that painter and frees all of their colour for you to take.
Use the walls. The fence is safe: no one can come from that side. Loops that run along the edge of the yard have one side less to defend.
Do not turn back on yourself. A sharp U-turn can run over your own trail. Make your turns a little wider.
Last ten seconds: the clock turns red. Only start a loop if you can close it before it reaches zero, because an open trail scores nothing.

title: Paint Grab FAQ
description: Answers about Paint Grab: is it free, is it online multiplayer, does it save, does it work on phones and Chromebooks, and why did my painter splat.
body: Is it free? Yes, it is free to play in the browser. There is nothing to buy: new painters and trails are unlocked with paint drops earned by playing.

Is it an online multiplayer game? No. The other painters are computer-controlled bots, so there is no chat, no strangers and no waiting for a server. It keeps working even on a slow connection once it has loaded.
Does it save my progress? Yes. Your best percentage, your paint drops, your shop items and your daily streak are stored in your browser (on CrazyGames, in your account).
Does it work on phones, in portrait and on Chromebooks? Yes. It plays with touch, mouse or keyboard, in portrait or landscape, and the download is about 1.6 MB.
Why did my painter splat? Someone touched your trail while you were outside your colour, you crossed your own trail, or you bumped heads with a painter who was standing in its own colour.

Is it a Paper.io copy? No. It is inspired by the territory mechanic of .io games, but it is a single-player game against bots with two-minute rounds, its own school-yard setting, characters, shop and art.
Can I turn the music off? Yes, with the speaker button in the top right corner.

title: Paint Grab for Schools and Kids – Safe, Short, No Sign-up
description: Paint Grab is a short, text-free territory game that runs on school Chromebooks: no chat, no online players, no purchases, no account and no personal data.
h1: Paint Grab for classrooms and kids
body: Paint Grab has no chat, no online players, no purchases, no account and no personal data. A round lasts two minutes, which makes it a good short reward between tasks.

There is no text in the game, so it works the same for children who are still learning to read and for students of any language. The only things on screen are numbers: a percentage, a clock and a place on the podium.

It quietly practises spatial thinking and risk management: players plan a loop, estimate how much area it will enclose, and decide when it is safe to go further and when to head home. The percentage counter is an easy way to talk about fractions and percentages of an area.
It runs in the browser on Chromebooks, tablets and phones, in portrait or landscape, and loads in a couple of seconds (about 1.6 MB).
